digest.headline: Platform and AI tooling, week 37
digest.intro: Three releases worth a look this week.

items.title: Dockhaven registry adds pull-through caching
items.summary: Dockhaven can act as a pull-through cache for other registries and keeps cached images for 30 days after the last pull.
items.whyItMatters: Cache hits do not count against the pull rate limit.

items.title: Anvilworks raises cache limits
items.summary: Anvilworks raises the maximum size of a single remote cache entry from 512 MB to 20 GB. Larger entries are stored in chunks and fetched in parallel.

items.title: Ploverly agents can stream tool results
items.summary: Ploverly 0.14 lets tools stream partial results back to the agent while they run, and the agent can stop a tool early once it has what it needs.

sources.title: Dockhaven registry adds pull-through caching
sources.summary: Dockhaven can now act as a pull-through cache for other registries. Cached images are kept for 30 days after the last pull. Cache hits do not count against the pull rate limit.

sources.title: Anvilworks raises cache limits
sources.summary: Anvilworks raises the maximum size of a single remote cache entry from 512 MB to 2 GB. Larger entries are stored in chunks and fetched in parallel. Existing caches need no migration.

sources.title: Ploverly agents can stream tool results
sources.summary: Ploverly 0.14 lets tools stream partial results back to the agent while they run. The agent can stop a tool early once it has what it needs. Streaming is opt-in per tool.
